text:
The Eagles have been far from perfect this season, but the NFC East is in a mess, and that means the postseason isn't out of reach. Keeping those hopes alive meant the Eagles couldn't afford to lose to the rival Cowboys on Thanksgiving afternoon, which quickly became an easier-said-than-done situation when star cornerback Cooper DeJean left the game in the first quarter.

DeJean was sent to the blue medical tent after a third-down play in the opening frame, and while Eagles fans hoped the worst was dodged, that wasn't the case. Should Philadelphia be worried about the 23-year-old defensive playmaker's outlook moving forward?

Let's break down the latest on DeJean's injury as each update unfolds.

Analyzing Cooper DeJean's injury

DeJean picked up a head injury when attempting to tackle Cowboys running back Javonte Williams on a third-down conversion attempt in the first defensive series. It wasn't long before the Eagles confirmed fans' worst fears when they officially ruled DeJean out at 5 p.m. ET, declaring that he had been diagnosed with a concussion.

Every player deals with concussions differently, so there isn't a set timeframe for when the Eagles can expect DeJean to return. Some players are concussed and don't end up missing time, while others' seasons can be completely derailed because of a concussion.

Either way, the former 2024 second-rounder must clear the NFL's five-stage concussion protocol before returning to Philadelphia's secondary.

Stage 1: Symptom-limited activity

Stage 2: Aerobic exercises

Stage 3: Football-specific exercises

Stage 4: Team-based non-contact drills

Stage 5: Full football activity

Given that DeJean hasn't even been cleared for the first stage, it's hard to predict when he'll return.

Although you never want to see a player hurt, perhaps some time away is needed. After playing to career-worst overall (53.2) and coverage (50.5) Pro Football Focus grades through the Eagles' first 11 games of the season—including before he got hurt on Thanksgiving. He's allowed 32 receptions on 51 targets for 402 yards and three touchdowns, with two pass break-ups and one interception.

Cooper DeJean injury history

DeJean has been reliably healthy throughout the early part of his NFL career. Even though he hasn't played a full season yet, he only missed one game in each of the two previous seasons and hadn't missed any action this year until he was concussed against the Cowboys.

Before becoming a pro, DeJean experienced a season-ending fibula break in his final year at Iowa. The injury is clearly behind him, and it's more than safe to say it has no connection to Thursday afternoon's concussion.

That said, it'll be interesting to see if it's a one-off issue or if concussions will be something that plagues DeJean more regularly moving forward.

Eagles' plan without Cooper DeJean

Once DeJean left the game, veteran defensive back Michael Carter II took over his role in the Eagles' secondary. Philadelphia has used the Duke product as a safety more often than not this season, but his extensive slot experience (2,298 career snaps) has made him DeJean's de facto replacement.

He isn't exactly known for his coverage, but Carter has been solid against the pass this season, playing to a 63.1 PFF coverage grade—his best effort since 2023 (83.3). He's allowed only 4-of-8 targets for 22 yards and a 56.3 passer rating, which should give the Eagles a sense of relief until DeJean returns.

Considering how Carter will be a free agent in March, let's hope he's motivated enough to not only secure his future but also help the Eagles for as long as DeJean is sidelined.

text:
The Green Bay Packers struggled to overcome the absence of Christian Watson after the wide receiver exited their matchup against the Los Angeles Rams with a concussion. The injury came at an unfortunate time as they're already trying to recover from a difficult stretch following consecutive losses. However, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur offered an encouraging update on Watson's condition after the team's 26-13 loss to Los Angeles.

LaFleur revealed that he believes Watson is currently “in a good place” following the concussion but admitted that he is unsure about the receiver's exact status in the league's concussion protocol.

Watson sustained the injury after taking a hard hit from Rams star Kamren Kinchens while attempting to haul in a pass near the sideline. The collision sent the Packers wide receiver to the ground for several moments.

Kinchens was subsequently ejected from the game for the hit, while Watson was escorted to the locker room for a concussion evaluation.

The Packers struggled to move the ball effectively after losing Watson, and LaFleur didn't hesitate to acknowledge how much his absence affected the offense.

“I think you need your best players out there,” he said. “When they're not out there, it certainly hurts your chances. He's a guy that's tough to replace.”

Watson's absence was particularly noticeable considering the impact he had made before leaving the game. The Packers receiver recorded four receptions for 65 yards and a touchdown in the first half.

However, Green Bay struggled to generate much offense after losing him. Turnover problems also continued to haunt the Packers throughout the night. Green Bay has now committed seven turnovers over its last two games, its highest total in a two-game span since 2007. LaFleur also pointed to the team's ball-security problems as a major factor behind the disappointing defeat.

The Packers have an extended break between their Wednesday night meeting with the Rams and their next game. The additional recovery time could work in Watson's favor. However, his availability will ultimately depend on how he progresses through the concussion protocol and whether he receives medical clearance.

Philadelphia Eagles star RB Saquon Barkley left the NFL game against the Dallas Cowboys. He is the 3rd Eagles star to leave the game so far in the early going. Dallas Goedert and Cooper DeJean also left the game earlier. DeJean will not return, while Goedert is questionable to return.

MORE: Bold predictions for Week 12 of 2026 NFL season

Barkley was already injured before game

Barkley exited Philadelphia's Week 11 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit on a five-yard run. He did not return, and the initial concern was an injury to his left arm.

The Eagles later listed Barkley with a neck injury and an illness. He was limited in Monday's estimated practice report before upgrading to full participation Tuesday and Wednesday.

Philadelphia's final injury report did not include Barkley, meaning he was cleared for the Week 12 game against Dallas.

Saquon Barkley (stinger) is questionable to return to Thursday's Week 12 game against the Dallas Cowboys

This is a concerning development for the Philadelphia Eagles, particularly because Barkley had dealt with a possible stinger earlier in the season.

Barkley's availability for the remainder of Thursday's matchup will depend on how he responds to the injury evaluation. If he cannot return, Philadelphia will need to rely more heavily on its other running backs.

A stinger can affect a player's shoulder, arm, and neck, making his ability to return uncertain. For now, the Eagles will lean on RB Will Shipley to hold down the backfield, and they will be relying on QB Joe Milton to lead the offense.

On the Eagles' first drive without Barkley, they did get into field goal range, and Barkley was seen on the sidelines itching to get back into the game. The score is now 14-3 for the Cowboys with about half the 2nd quarter remaining.

text:
Quarterback Brock Purdy missed his second day of practice in a row, bringing into question his status to play in the 49ers’ important matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.

Purdy sustained an ankle injury in the second quarter of the 49ers’ 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday. He remained in the game and played well enough to be named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.

The 49ers lead the NFC West with a conference-best record of 9-1. The Seahawks, last season’s Super Bowl champions, enter the week 6-4 and battling for a spot in the postseason.

Backup quarterback Mac Jones would be in line to make his first start of the season if Purdy is not available to play on Sunday at Levi’s Stadium.

Jones has completed his only pass this season for 5 yards. Last year, Jones started eight games. He completed 69.6% of his pass attempts for 2,151 yards with 13 touchdowns, six interceptions and a passer rating of 97.4.

On Wednesday, coach Kyle Shanahan said it was possible that Purdy could miss the Week 12 game against the Seahawks.

“It's not a high ankle so it's day-to-day with it, but we’ve got to see how it goes,” Shanahan said.

San Francisco 49ers

Find the latest San Francisco 49ers news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Bay Area and California.

Purdy is having an exceptional season for the 49ers. Purdy has thrown 23 touchdown passes with five interceptions. He leads the NFL with a passer rating of 118.2.

Wide receiver Mike Evans returned to limited practice on Thursday, while Jordan Watkins remained sidelined with a groin injury.

Offensive lineman Austen Pleasants was a full participant in practice. The 49ers opened the practice window for him on Wednesday. He has been on injured reserve since Week 1. Pleasants could be activated to serve as the 49ers’ backup tackle with Vederian Lowe taking over at right tackle. Bears tight end Cole Kmet had a season-ending knee injury last month.

text:
DETROIT -- DETROIT (AP) — Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland was carted off the field with a knee injury in the first quarter against the Detroit Lions on Thursday in another setback at the position.

Loveland limped off the field and after being evaluated on the sideline, he was transported to the locker room with a towel covering his face and was ruled out shortly thereafter. The former Michigan star had one catch for 5 yards and lost a fumble at Ford Field.

Bears tight end Cole Kmet had a season-ending knee injury last month.

After Chicago outlasted Detroit for a 39-35 win, quarterback Caleb Williams had his midsection examined after he was sacked four times.

“Nothing showed up on the scans,” Williams said.

Before the game kicked off, the Lions were down two more starters on defense and Chicago was missing one starter on that side of the ball.

Lions edge rusher DJ Wonnum (back) and safety Chuck Clark (hamstring) were ruled out on Thursday as well as Chicago defensive back Kyler Gordon (shoulder) because of injuries.

The Bears previously ruled out backup defensive back Elijah Hicks (concussion) on Wednesday.

Detroit’s defense has been improving lately despite losing All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell and Pro Bowl edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to season-ending injuries.

text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without safety Kamren Kinchens for the second half of Wednesday's game, while the Green Bay Packers will be without wide receiver Christian Watson.

Kitchens launched himself at Watson on a fourth-down play late in the second quarter. ESPN's Rob Demovsky reported he was ejected for the hit that left Watson "down for an extended period of time" before the receiver eventually walked away from the situation under his own power.

Green Bay announced Watson was ruled out because of a concussion.

While the pass was incomplete, the Packers kept the ball because of offsetting penalties.

Kinchens was flagged for the hit, but Green Bay wide receiver Matthew Golden was penalized for offensive pass interference. With Watson not on the field, the visitors decided to kick the field goal on their second chance at the fourth down.

Kinchens entered play with 40 tackles, one interception and a half sack on the season.

As for Watson, he is one of the most important players in Green Bay's offense. That was clear in the first half, as he scored the Packers' lone touchdown to go with 65 receiving yards on four catches.

He entered play Wednesday leading Green Bay with 916 receiving yards and seven touchdown catches thanks in large part to his ability to beat defenses over the top with his speed and come down with contested catches.

If Watson is sidelined for extended time, quarterback Jordan Love will need to rely on Golden even more than he already does. The Watson and Golden combination is one of the best one-two punches in the league and critical to Love's deep-passing attack.

DETROIT — The Detroit Lions listed five players as inactive on the final injury report ahead of their Week 12 matchup against the red-hot Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day inside Ford Field.
The Lions, at 8-2, are riding a six-game winning streak as their defense is holding opposing offenses to under 21 points per game during this stretch.
text:
What to know:

Game day: Thanksgiving Day.

Kickoff: 1 p.m. ET.

Location: Ford Field in Detroit.

Lions record: 8-2, riding a six-game winning streak.

Bears record: 8-2, riding a five-game winning streak.

Both teams are hot: This is a major NFC North showdown between two 8-2 teams.

DETROIT — The Detroit Lions listed five players as inactive on the final injury report ahead of their Week 12 matchup against the red-hot Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day inside Ford Field.

The Lions, at 8-2, are riding a six-game winning streak as their defense is holding opposing offenses to under 21 points per game during this stretch.

But coming into town are former offensive coordinator and current head coach of the Bears, Ben Johnson, former running back D’Andre Swift, and former Michigan Wolverines national champion Colston Loveland, who are sitting on an 8-2 record while riding a five-game winning streak behind a top-notch defense and the impeccable arm of Caleb Williams in the process.

Jeffery Simmons, whom the Bears just acquired through trade, has five sacks in three games, and will try to get to Lions quarterback Jared Goff, who has Penei Sewell to protect him in the pocket.

This week’s inactive players have been announced.

Although Sewell will be on the offensive line, the Lions have lost top rookie Cade Mays to an ankle injury, which put him on injured reserve.

Earlier this week, the Lions announced that defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard will miss the rest of the season after suffering a knee injury that will require surgery following the Lions’ victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Here’s the full injury report:

Cornerback Keith Abney II -- out (healthy scratch).

Safety Chuck Clark -- out (hamstring).

Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. -- out (shoulder).

Edge Tyrus Wheat -- out (healthy scratch).

Edge DJ Wonnum -- out (back injury).

Kickoff is at 1 p.m.

text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are seemingly preparing for the possibility of being without starting quarterback Justin Herbert against the New England Patriots on Sunday.

The Chargers announced Thursday that they signed veteran quarterback Jake Browning from the practice squad to the active roster.

Herbert is currently in concussion protocol, and if he is not cleared in time to play against New England, the Chargers will likely turn to DJ Uiagalelei at quarterback with Browning as the backup.

Browning, 30, entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie out of the University of Washington in 2019, and he has bounced around between multiple organizations since then.

After a stint on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad to start his career, Browning was with the Cincinnati Bengals from 2021 to 2025, and that is where he first saw regular-season game action.

In 2023, Browning went 4-3 in seven starts for the Bengals, completing a league-high 70.4 percent of his passes for 1,936 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

Browning also made three starts for Cincinnati last season, but he largely struggled, going 0-3, and completing 64.8 percent of his passing attempts for 771 yards, six touchdowns and eight picks.

After spending time with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the preseason, Browning was released, and he was signed to the Chargers' practice squad in October.

The Chargers are coming off a 27-24 loss to the New York Jets last week, which dropped them to 1-9 on the season.

Herbert, who accounted for three total touchdowns in the defeat, was placed in concussion protocol on Monday.

If Herbert cannot play on Sunday, it would put Uiagalelei in line for his first career NFL regular-season start.

Uiagalelei saw his first regular-season game action on Nov. 8 when he went 2-of-7 for 24 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in a 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans.

text:
The Chicago Bears lost one of Caleb Williams' top targets to a worrisome injury in their Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Detroit Lions, as tight end Colston Loveland exited the game in the first half.

Loveland's injury occurred on the Bears' second offensive drive, after he'd been blocking for D'Andre Swift on a run. Loveland got tangled up with with Lions linebackers Trevor Nowaske and Malcolm Rodriguez on the play. Replays appeared to show Lions defensive tackle Tyleik Williams pushing Loveland as the Bears tight end attempted to regain his balance.

Loveland got up and limped off the field on his own before visiting the blue medical tent. He was subsequently carted to the locker room with a left knee injury and ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Read More on NFL

After the incident, Jeff Mueller, a physical therapist and NFL injury analyst, wrote on X, "Primary concern: MCL Secondary concern: ACL, but hopefully wasn’t enough valgus+rotation stress. Looks like his foot is externally rotated so can’t rule it out unfortunately."

Earlier in the game, Loveland had a costly fumble on the Bears' opening drive, and the Lions were able to jump out to an early 10-0 lead. He had one catch for five yards before leaving the game.

More news: Packers’ Jordan Love Gets Brutally Honest After Two-Interception Game

The Bears (9-2), which went on to win the game 39-35, were already without another of their top tight ends. Cole Kmet was placed on season-ending injured reserve last month due to a right knee injury against the New England Patriots.

Loveland's exit meant the Bears would have to rely on backups Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson at the position.

Roush is a 6-foot-6 rookie whom the Bears selected in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft from Stanford. He's taken the top spot on the team's tight end depth chart due to Kmet and Loveland's injuries.

Carlson is a veteran tight end the Bears signed earlier this month. He also helped out after Loveland's injury, including catching several passes from Williams on the Bears' first half-scoring drive. Carlson had two catches for 30 yards before halftime, while Roush had one reception for seven yards.

Loveland, selected No. 10 by the Bears in the 2025 NFL draft, played in 16 games for Chicago last season, starting in 11. The former Michigan standout appeared in each of the Bears' first 10 games this season, but his availability for their next game is now uncertain.

Depending on the severity of Loveland's injury, the Bears might need to sign another tight end to bolster their depleted depth at the position.

text:
DETROIT -- Bears tight end Colston Loveland has been ruled out for the rest of Chicago's Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Lions after injuring his left knee in the first quarter.

Loveland was hurt while blocking on D'Andre Swift's 2-yard run on the Bears' second offensive series with 6:15 remaining in the quarter.

Loveland was engaged in a block with Lions linebacker Trevor Nowaske and got rolled up by linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez at the end of the play. He hobbled off the field under his own power and went to the medical tent for evaluation before being carted to the locker room with a towel over his head.

The Bears announced at the beginning of the second quarter that Loveland would not return.

On the previous series -- Chicago's first drive of the game -- Loveland caught a 5-yard pass and made his way into the red zone before Detroit rookie defensive end Derrick Moore punched the ball out from under Loveland's arm. It was the tight end's second lost fumble since Week 8 at Seattle.

The Bears were already thin at tight end after Cole Kmet sustained a season-ending knee injury late in Chicago's Week 7 win against the New England Patriots. Chicago's remaining active tight ends in Detroit are rookie Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson.

Loveland has 40 catches for 392 yards and three touchdowns through 10 games. He ranks third on the team in receiving yards.

text:
Los Angeles Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's 26-13 win against the Green Bay Packers.

Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love was trying to float a pass to the sideline, targeting Christian Watson.

The Packers wideout looked over his shoulder to track the ball, and Kinchens came out of nowhere and laid a massive, unexpected hit on Watson.

He was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson, and the wide receiver remained down on the field, needing to be tended to by trainers. Watson was ruled out with a concussion.

Kinchens finished the first Thanksgiving eve game with just one tackle and two pass deflections. He will look to return next week when Los Angeles takes on the Kansas City Chiefs for "Thursday Night Football" next week.

This was the second injury Watson has dealt with in this game. On his first reception for 6 yards on the Packers' opening drive, he left the field and was questionable to return with a thigh injury. He returned on Green Bay's next possession.

Watson scored the Packers' first touchdown of the game in the second quarter. Love found him for the 6-yard score to help bring Green Bay within three points.

Watson has been no stranger to injuries this season. He left the team's Week 8 game against the Carolina Panthers with a broken rib. Watson was taken to a local hospital during the game, but returned to the stadium in an ambulance, still wearing his gear, and ran back onto the field to return to the game.

The Packers wide receiver finished that game with 113 yards on six receptions.

Thanksgiving Eve hasn't gone according to plan for Christian Watson.

The Green Bay Packers receiver exited with a thigh injury after making his first catch of the game. He returned on the Packers' second drive. Watson appeared to be in the clear, until taking a huge hit late in the first half from the Los Angeles Rams' Kamren Kinchens.

Watson remained down after the play, where his head hit the turf.

Kinchens was ejected from the game. Officials determined that the defender left his feet and delivered a forceable blow to the head and/or neck area.

The 27-year-old Watson has been no stranger to injuries in his career, but has remained healthy in what has been a career-year for him.

Here's the latest on Watson.

Christian Watson injury update

The Packers say that Watson is being evaluated for a concussion and his return is questionable. Watson was able to get up and walk off the field.

He returned to the game earlier after being listed as questionable to return with a thigh injury, the Packers announced.

It's far from an ideal situation for the Packers, who are already playing without their star running back, Josh Jacobs, and their No. 2 receiver, Jayden Reed.

With injuries also along the offensive line, the Packers' offense is being forced to overcome a lot this season.

Packers WR depth chart

Christian Watson

Matthew Golden

Savion Williams

Skyy Moore

Bo Melton

J. Michael Sturdivant

The situation is getting dire for the Green Bay receiver room. Without Watson, the Packers will be relying on the speedster, Golden, to take on the bulk of the work. Williams, a third-round pick in 2025, has proven to be a weapon for Matt LaFleur's offense, but hasn't seen the same volume that Watson and Golden are used to.

text:
The New England Patriots have spent much of Thanksgiving week dealing with the uncertainty surrounding their quarterback situation. However, Wednesday's initial injury report provided a reminder that the Los Angeles Chargers have considerable personnel concerns of their own. Among the 13 Chargers players who did not practice Wednesday was quarterback Justin Herbert, who is dealing with a concussion.

New England had four players miss Wednesday's practice, including quarterback Drake Maye, wide receiver A.J. Brown, cornerback Carlton Davis III and offensive lineman Walter Rouse. Neither team is particularly healthy entering Sunday's game, but the extent of Los Angeles' injury report introduces another interesting element to the Week 12 contest.

Chargers Have Concerns Beyond Justin Herbert

Herbert's availability will understandably dominate much of the conversation surrounding Los Angeles over the next several days. However, the Chargers also had several important defensive players unavailable Wednesday, including linebacker Daiyan Henley and edge rushers Akheem Mesidor and Tuli Tuipulotu. Veteran pass rusher Khalil Mack received a rest designation.

Those defensive situations are worth monitoring from New England's perspective. With Tommy DeVito expected to assume quarterback responsibilities in Maye's absence, the Patriots could benefit considerably from facing a defense that isn't operating at full strength. Keeping pressure away from DeVito would give offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels more flexibility when constructing his game plan.

Los Angeles also listed running back Keaton Mitchell and tight end David Njoku among its Wednesday absences. The initial report doesn't necessarily indicate which players will ultimately be unavailable Sunday, but it provides several developments worth following before the weekend.

MORE: Patriots Keys to Victory vs. Chargers in Week 12 NFL Game

Patriots Have Their Own Important Decisions Ahead

Brown's hamstring injury represents another concern for New England's offense. Fellow wide receiver Romeo Doubs participated on a limited basis Wednesday while dealing with a shoulder injury, creating additional uncertainty surrounding DeVito's potential supporting cast.

The Patriots did receive some encouraging news along their offensive line. Ben Brown participated fully despite appearing on the injury report with a knee issue, while Alijah Vera-Tucker managed limited participation.

Sunday's game could look considerably different depending on how both injury reports develop. New England has spent considerable time preparing for life without its starting quarterback, but the Chargers might also need to make significant adjustments.

For two teams approaching an important December stretch, Thanksgiving week's practice reports could prove particularly consequential.

text:
The Houston Texans have released their first injury report of the week rolling into their Week 12 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

And on the status for some players, things seem to be trending in the right direction. In the case of five others, they wound up not practicing on Wednesday, and thus makes their status a bit more cloudy as it relates to this weekend's action.

Let's break down the latest on the injury front from the Texans' practice a few days away from the Ravens traveling to Reliant Stadium:

Houston Texans Injury Report (as of 11/25)

DNP

TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot)

WR Kayshon Boutte (hip)

DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring)

OL Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder)

DT Sheldon Rankins (ankle)

LIMITED

WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring)

LB Jake Hummel (abdomen/groin)

DE Logan Hall (hip/shoulder)

FULL

CB Kamari Lassiter (wrist)

RB Woody Marks (concussion)

S Reed Blankenship (hand)

LB Jake Hansen (elbow)

OT Blake Fisher (thumb)

OT Trent Brown (wrist)

Let's break down some of the good news first: two of the Texans' bigger names on the offensive end that missed last week's game against the Colts managed to practice on Wednesday: that's running back Woody Marks (concussion) and wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring)

With two more days of practice to go for each, there's a good chance that both guys will be able to suit up against the Ravens considering everything continues to move in the right direction.

DeMeco Ryans noted that the team was "hopeful" Marks would make his return earlier this week, and signs appear to be pointing in that direction. Marks will pair up next to David Montgomery within the Texans' backfield, who came off a game where he posted his season-high in rushing yards with 107.

As for those that the Texans are at risk of being without on Sunday, though, there's a couple of names on each side of the ball to watch out for.

Most notably, defensive end Danielle Hunter still isn't practicing yet after suffering his hamstring injury before Week 10's game against the Cleveland Browns.

Houston will likely have to see Hunter practice once ahead of this coming weekend to have optimism around his playing status against Baltimore, but the team could be taking a rather cautious approach around one of their older, more impactful veterans on the defense.

Another older veteran on the Texans defense— defensive end Sheldon Rankins— also didn't practice on Wednesday.

Being without Hunter is enough of a challenge for Houston to overcome, but losing their top defensive tackle in Rankins could make things even tougher, if he is inevitably ruled out for this weekend. He's got two more days to practice and change the feelings around his status.

Offensively, the Texans had some concerns worth noting as well: wide receiver Kayshon Boutte is still dealing with the effects from his hip injury sustained on Thursday Night Football, and could put his status to play this weekend in doubt.

If Boutte is out, the Texans' wide receiver room will continue to look thin, as it has been since moving past the bye; relying on only Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson, and Marvin Harrison Jr., if he continues to trend in the right direction.

Keylan Rutledge is also still dealing with some of the effects of his injury suffered last week against the Colts, which turned out to be his second stinger of the year in the second half.

If Rutledge is set to miss any time moving forward, expect the Texans to roll with Febechi Nwaiwu as their fill-in at left guard. However, still with two more days of practice to go, there's still room for his and everyone else's status to improve between now and game day.

text:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. – Micah Parsons was filled with mixed feelings in the aftermath of his highly anticipated return Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams.

On one hand, Parsons felt healthy and strong while recording two quarterback hits and a sack in his first NFL game since tearing the anterior cruciate ligament and meniscus in his right knee 346 days ago in Denver.

While grateful to get through the game unscathed, Parsons also felt disappointment after coming up short during a 26-13 road loss to the Rams in Week 12 tilt at SoFi Stadium.

Knowing full well Los Angeles wanted to establish the run without star receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, Green Bay still struggled to contain the Rams' one-two punch of Blake Corum (32 carries for 184 yards and a touchdown) and Kyren Williams (12-46-1 TD) over four quarters.

The Rams controlled the ball for more than 40 minutes and nearly rushed for as many yards (241) on the ground as the Packers had in total (244).

"We all saw that game, and we saw where we got exploited at," Parsons said. "It starts with us. It starts with up front. It's not pointing fingers at things but when runs open up like the Red Sea, we gotta look at ourselves in the mirror regardless of how that is. We have to do a better job collectively up front."

Green Bay kept a lid on the Rams' offense early, limiting it to two Brandon McManus field goals in the first quarter despite a sudden-change situation in Packers' territory.

Momentum seemed to swing in Green Bay's favor in the second quarter. The Packers' offense tied the game up at 13 and Parsons sacked Stafford for an 8-yard loss in the final two minutes of the half.

Corum had just seven carries for 23 yards in the first half with Williams adding two runs for 12 yards, but the game seemed to turn on a 14-play, 64-yard touchdown-producing drive at the start of the third quarter that included four third-down conversions and ate 8 minutes off the clock.

After the two teams traded interceptions, Corum started to build steam as the Rams methodically wore down Green Bay's defensive front. In the fourth quarter, Corum busted runs of 29 and 35 yards to support point-producing drives.

It's not the first time the Packers have struggled to stop a rushing offense this season. Bijan Robinson rushed 29 times for 194 yards and two TDs in Atlanta's 35-14 win over Green Bay in its home opener back in September.

"I think that last part just comes down to, we need to figure out who's going to be a dawg or not. Like that's just the reality of it," Parsons said. "If someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don't have an answer for it, that's accountability.

"We've got to figure out who's willing to play with us or who's playing against us at this point because every quarter, every minute, every down matters and we've got to figure out who's in this for the long haul and who's in it for the ride."

The Packers kept Parsons on a rep count, playing 26 of the 71 total defensive snaps. He still had his trademark burst while recording two of Green Bay's three hits on Stafford and the defense's lone sack. He was credited with four total pressures.

"I'm thankful that I was able to play again and be with my friends and my brothers as teammates," Parsons said. "But as the competitor, I'm just highly, highly disappointed with how we performed collectively.

"We knew it would be a run- and screen-dominant game because of who they were missing. We just didn't play good enough as a front and I hold myself accountable in that process. We just have to be better."

Watson leaves with concussion: The Packers breathed a collective sigh of relief after a scary incident near the end of the first half when Rams safety Kamren Kinchens laid out Packers receiver Christian Watson with a helmet-to-helmet hit.

Watson eventually walked to the locker room under his own power but was ruled out due to a concussion. Kinchens was ejected for the hit.

"I turned around, I seen it last minute," receiver Matthew Golden said. "I don't know if it was a dirty hit or what, but obviously you hate to see one of your guys go down like that. I was just praying for him in the moment and was just hoping he got back up."

Watson played a critical role in Green Bay putting 13 points on the board early, catching four passes for 65 yards and a 6-yard touchdown in the first half alone.

The Packers struggled to move the ball without Watson in the second half, recording only 55 total yards of offense and no points.

"It was definitely a blow," safety Evan Williams said. "Anytime you have a player like that, and he goes down for the game, and we'll see when we get him back. Obviously, it hurts the morale initially but at the same time, as a professional football club, you gotta find a way to bounce back. You gotta find a way to shake whatever feelings you feel about that."

Packers need wins: Both Parsons and Williams acknowledged the need for Green Bay to get on a run after back-to-back losses to Minnesota and now the Rams.

Sitting at 6-5, the Packers are now on the outside looking in on in the NFC playoff race – 2½ games behind Detroit in the NFC North division and a game behind L.A. for the No. 7 seed.

"This hole is massive," Parsons said. "We took a big swing and we missed ginormously. The only way to get out is we probably have to win out. That's just the reality of this situation. I think the people know that. We know that. From player to coach, we have to play better. It's not just the players. It's coaches, the whole thing, we have to all be better."

The Packers travel to face New Orleans in Week 13 before playing four of their last five regular-season games at home.

"It's critical that we play our best football every time we're on the field now," Williams said. "Otherwise, we might not be sniffing the playoffs. I think it starts with everybody taking their own accountability, looking in the mirror and just finding ways to get better."

text:
The Chicago Bears have released their final injury report on the day before the Week 12 game against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving.

As they did the previous two days, the Bears held a walk-through once again, so the injury report is an estimation for the third consecutive day.

The final injury report includes a new addition for the second straight day, and that player, along with another, is listed as questionable.

As for players ruled out, there are three in total. We'll go over all of that and much more after checking out the injury report for Wednesday.

Bears' Wednesday injury report

A new addition among 2 questionable

Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson is a new addition to the injury report with a groin injury and, along with linebacker D'Marco Jackson, he is questionable to play on Thursday.

Assuming he didn't somehow injure himself during the walk-through, the fact that Stevenson was listed as limited gives Chicago's cornerback a chance to suit up.

As for Jackson, three full practices suggests he will go.

3 Bears ruled out

As expected, defensive back Kyler Gordon, safety Elijah Hicks and running back Roschon Johnson have been ruled out.

The writing was on the wall with both Gordon and Johnson after they were estimated non-participants on Monday and Tuesday.

Gordon got hurt before the bye, and Johnson was carted off with his injury during the Week 11 game against the New Orleans Saints. This is now two missed games in a row for Gordon.

Hicks popped up on the injury report on Tuesday and was ruled out immediately by head coach Ben Johnson due to his concussion.

That situation is a little strange because Hicks was not reported to have a concussion during or after last week's game and Chicago didn't hold a full practice this week.

That said, sometimes players don't start getting symptoms until a day or two after a game, so that's probably the case here.

How Bears will replace Gordon, Johnson, Hicks

The Bears have a few options to replace Gordon, assuming Stevenson overcomes the questionable tag.

One of them is to put Malik Muhammad in the slot and have Stevenson on the outside. Muhammad played very good football in the slot earlier in the season while Gordon was out with a calf issue.

The other option is to run it back with Clark Phillips, who played in the slot against the Saints and had himself a great game.

There would be a third option in Cam Lewis, but with Hicks ruled out, the Bears need Lewis at safety next to Dillon Thieneman.

Rookie Skyler Thomas is in line to be the primary backup at safety with Hicks sidelined, but the Bears also need a new punt protector, which was Hicks' other job. Thomas, Salvon Ahmed and Marlew Sewell, who was re-signed to the practice squad this week, all received looks in that role during the preseason.

Speaking of Ahmed, he will be Chicago's RB3 with Johnson out.

text:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for a hit along the sideline that left Packers wide receiver Christian Watson with a concussion Wednesday night.

The play came on a fourth-and-1 late in the second quarter, when Kinchens left his feet and launched into Watson while leading with his head.

Watson was down long enough that medical personnel came across the field with a gurney, but it was not needed. Watson got up and walked to the locker room. He was ruled out because of the concussion at the start of the second half.

After the game, Kinchens said he was "just trying to play fast."

"I came with no ill intent," Kinchens said. "I wasn't trying to hurt anyone or nothing like that. Just was trying to get an incomplete pass. It was fourth-and-1, bang-bang play."

Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he did not get a good look at the hit on Watson but came away encouraged after talking to the wide receiver after the game.

"Yeah, it seems like he's in a good place, but where he's at in terms of the protocol, I don't know," LaFleur said.

Kinchens was initially called for unnecessary roughness then ejected after a video review.

"I hope Watson is OK," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "I know [Kinchens'] heart. I mean, and all of our guys, they try to do the best job they can, finding that strike zone, keeping their head out of the tackle. I was bummed for him, and I'm also hopeful that Watson is OK because that's the worst part of this game when you see guys get injured. You never want to see that, but the call came from New York, so obviously they saw something that they felt like was in alignment for the ejection."

The Packers managed only two first downs after Watson was injured, and both came on their second-to-last drive, which ended in Jordan Love's second interception. The Packers ran just 16 plays in the second half and had the ball for just six minutes and 15 seconds.

"It sucked to lose him on that play," Love said. "I know he wished he could be out there with us but it's just one of those things where we talk about it all the time, the next-man-up mentality. Obviously, he's a big part of our offense. You could see in the first half, he was making some big, big plays. Obviously was a huge part of what we were leaning on today and we weren't able to overcome when he went out of the game."

Kinchens reached a maximum speed of 18.41 mph on the play, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He is the first Rams player disqualified from a game since Puka Nacua was ejected in Week 9 of the 2024 season against the Seattle Seahawks.

Watson had four receptions for 65 yards and his career-best eighth touchdown of the season before exiting. The Rams silenced the Watson-less Packers in the second half, holding them scoreless in a 26-13 win.

Less than a month ago, Watson left the Week 8 game against the Carolina Panthers only to return to the matchup after a trip to the hospital. Tests showed Watson fractured a rib but suffered no other injuries.

text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without one of their safeties for the remainder of Wednesday night, while the Green Bay Packers will be sans their top wide receiver.

Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was disqualified for an illegal hit on Packers wideout Christian Watson with 1:54 to play in the first half of Wednesday night’s Week 12 game. Watson was ruled out at the opening of the second half with a concussion.

Per the Netflix broadcast, the call to eject Kinchens came from the New York office and NFL executive vice president Troy Vincent for Kinchens leaving his feet and making helmet-to-helmet contact.

On fourth-and-1, Packers quarterback Jordan Love lofted a pass toward the sideline. Watson was tracking it and was laid out by Kinchens.

Watson remained down on the sideline before walking under his own power to be evaluated for a concussion and was deemed questionable to return before he was eventually ruled out.

The play didn’t result in a penalty, however, as it was offset by an offensive pass interference call against the Packers’ Matthew Golden. Green Bay's Trey Smack kicked a game-tying field goal on the ensuing play.

The Packers and Rams were tied, 13-13, at halftime.

Kinchens, who’s played in nine games with four starts, had a tackle and two pass breakups at the time of his ejection.

Watson had game highs of four receptions and 65 yards, including the Packers’ only touchdown – a 6-yard catch from Love with 8:06 to play in the second quarter -- when he exited.

Watson memorably returned to play in Week 8 in a Thursday night matchup against the Carolina Panthers in which he emerged from an ambulance after being transported to a hospital for precautionary reasons.

text:
FOXBORO — Drake Maye won't play this week, the first time in his three-year NFL career that the New England Patriots quarterback won't be active for a game. Since his fibula injury two weeks ago, Maye hasn't practiced with the 5-5 Patriots, who are looking to try and right the ship heading into the stretch run.

In their way is the Los Angeles Chargers, who are tied for the league's worst record at 1-9 and don't have much going for them. Both sides are trying to snap a losing streak and claw their way back into the conversation.

But injuries remain a big storyline for New England going into the weekend.

Here's a look at the Patriots' initial injury report for Week 12, which has a number of big-name guys listed.

On the other side, the Chargers have just as many key players listed on their injury report — including their starting quarterback who might end up missing the game entirely.

It's Tommy DeVito's Show

Nope, the Patriots won't be adding another quarterback this week, so it's been all DeVito in practice as he ramps up for his first start with the team. He's going to be backed up by rookie Behren Morton, who's now been elevated to the QB2 role.

Maye has been in the facility, according to Mike Vrabel, but his status for the remainder of 2026 remains up in the air as he continues to try and heal from his fractured fibula. The door hasn't been shut on his potential return, but for now, he remains on the active roster instead of moving to injured reserve.

Now DeVito will lead the Patriots into battle on Sunday afternoon knowing he'll be playing.

"Prep, yeah," DeVito said this week about what he's doing differently this week. "I think just more meeting time with Josh (McDaniels) and Ash(ton Grant), and just going over the game plan a little bit more in that regard. And then just going from there."

Vera-Tucker, Doubs Return

This week, the Patriots got some offensive help back onto the field. Offensive guard Alijah Vera-Tucker returned from IR, starting his 21-day window to be activated to the 53-man roster. The starting left guard has missed the last four games and should help solidify a banged-up offensive line.

Additionally, the Patriots also had wide receiver Romeo Doubs make his return to practice after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 6. The big-time free agent acquisition, like AVT, has three weeks to be added to the active roster.

The Patriots' roster is full at 53 players right now, so if either player (or both) get added this weekend, it would need to come after a pair of corresponding moves. Walter Rouse, who missed last game with a concussion and hasn't practiced with his teammates this week, could be a candidate to land on IR.

Who Starts For LA at QB?

It's not just New England who could turn to a backup quarterback. Justin Herbert entered concussion protocol last week and didn't speak to reporters after the Chargers' loss to the Jets, meaning that backup D.J. Uiagalelei might end up making his first start.

"Yeah, he hasn't had a lot of exposure this year," Vrabel said Tuesday. "So, just like any other backup quarterback in the National Football League, they're preparing for their opportunity and whatever that may look like and however that may go. It's no different than where we're at with our situation and where we've been, and go from there."

Herbert needs to clear five stages of the NFL's concussion protocol before being allowed to suit up, so until he's able to play, we could end up seeing DeVito vs. Uiagalelei in a game that was (smartly) flexed out of Sunday Night Football.

Key Defensive Back Returns to Practice

In the first two practices of the week, the Patriots were without Craig Woodson. On Wednesday, he returned to the field in a full capacity.

The second-year safety has been a really important player for this defense, playing in all, but one game and nabbing a game-sealing interception in the final moments of the Patriots' Week 4 win in Buffalo.

With Carlton Davis missing practice Wednesday, having the secondary get someone back is a good sign for a unit that's had a rough few games.

Five Denver Broncos players are eligible to return from injury lists this week.

Denver running back Tyler Badie (thumb) and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) are eligible to return from injured reserve, but it sounds like Elliss likely needs more time to recover.

Meanwhile, Denver offensive tackle Frank Crum (leg) and tight end Caleb Lohner (lower body) have both been eligible to return from injured reserve since Week 5, and Lohner opened his 21-day window to be activated last week. Offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo (knee) has also been eligible to return from the reserve/physically unable to perform list for several weeks.

NFL clubs are allowed to designate up to eight players to return from IR during the regular season, and two of those designations were used on Crum and Lohner when the initial 53-man roster was set this summer. The Broncos have already brought back running back Jonah Coleman and wide receiver Pat Bryant, so the club can designate up to four more players to return this fall.

RB Tyler Badie (thumb)

OL Nick Gargiulo (knee)

text:
The San Francisco 49ers had some unexpected news Wednesday as they began their preparation for Sunday’s game against the rival Seattle Seahawks.

Quarterback Brock Purdy missed Wednesday’s practice due to an ankle injury he suffered in the second quarter of Sunday’s 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings, head coach Kyle Shanahan said.

The injury puts Purdy’s status in question ahead of Sunday’s game as the 49ers look to take a stranglehold of the NFC West. They’re 9-1 and enter the weekend with a three-game lead over the second-place Seahawks with a chance to win the head-to-head tiebreaker with six games remaining.

“We’ll see. He can’t go today,” Shanahan said before practice.

Shanahan said he knew Purdy was hurt from the training staff, who cleared him to stay in the game.

“They always tell you when someone has something,” Shanahan said. “But then they came back and said, ‘Yeah, he checked out, he should be fine.'”

Purdy played the second half with his ankles taped while the 49ers pulled away from the Vikings’ top-ranked defense in Mexico City. Purdy completed 21 of 26 for 255 yards and 3 touchdowns, strengthening his case for MVP candidacy.

Purdy earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors for the fourth time in his career. His 146.0 passer rating against Minnesota marked the seventh time he’s posted a rating of at least 145, the most by any quarterback in his first five NFL seasons.

Purdy’s ability to sidestep pressure and keep his eyes downfield buys receivers time to uncover, an edge San Francisco could lose if his ankle limits him against Seattle.

If Purdy can’t play Sunday, the 49ers would turn to Mac Jones, who kept San Francisco’s season afloat in 2025 when Purdy missed eight games with a turf toe injury. The 49ers went 5-3 in Jones’ starts while finishing the season 12-5.

They were in the mix for the No. 1 seed all the way until the regular season finale when they lost to Seattle, who also beat the 49ers in the Divisional Round of the playoffs to end their season.

text:
The NFL is in the midst of its most chaotic week of the season. Due to the Thanksgiving holiday, we've embarked on a six-day stretch that includes five days of games. While the Packers and Rams get things started on Wednesday night, we still have the Thanksgiving triple-header and the Black Friday game before we even start talking about the regular Sunday slate and, of course, Monday Night Football.

When you sprinkle in some utter madness between Aaron Rodgers and his now-former team, the Pittsburgh Steelers, there will be plenty to talk about around the dinner table this holiday season.

Of course, one of the topics of conversation will also be injuries. They're an omnipresent aspect of the NFL and are a factor as we step into Week 12. Below, we examine every injury report across the league, as well as highlight the game statuses for Thanksgiving.

All games are Sunday unless noted.

Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions (Thursday)

Bears: DB Kyler Gordon (shoulder), DB Elijah Hicks (concussion), RB Roschon Johnson (ankle) OUT; DB Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (groin), LB D'Marco Jackson (elbow) QUESTIONABLE

Lions: DL Skyler Gill-Howard (knee), CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) OUT; S Chuck Clark (hamstring), EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) QUESTIONABLE

While Wednesday's practice was conducted as a walk-through, Tyrique Stevenson Sr. did pop up on the injury report with a groin injury. He was limited for the session and officially listed as questionable.

Gill Howard nor Rakestraw practiced this week, so it's not surprising to see them ruled out. On a more positive note, Chuck Clark returned to practice on Tuesday and remained a limited participant during Wednesday's session. Moreover, pass rusher DJ Wonnum was limited on Wednesday after missing the first two practices of the week with a back injury.

Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (Thursday)

Eagles: OLB Arnold Ebiketie (oblique), CB Jonathan Jones (ankle) OUT

Cowboys: G Tyler Booker (ankle), TE Jake Ferguson (knee, ankle), DB P.J. Locke (concussion), WR Jonathan Mingo (ankle) OUT; CB Devin Moore (hip), DB Jalen Thompson (hamstring) QUESTIONABLE

Quinyon Mitchell carries no game designation, so the Eagles star corner is slated to play. He was a full participant during Wednesday's practice after missing Monday's session and being limited on Tuesday due to a hamstring injury.

Dak Prescott was listed on the injury report this week with a left hand injury, but the Cowboys quarterback was a full participant throughout and has no game designation. Meanwhile, Booker and Ferguson did not practice at all this week and will be sidelined for Week 12.

Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (Thursday)

Chiefs: RB Kenneth Walker III (groin), OL Jaylon Moore (ankle), DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) OUT; TE Noah Gray (rib), DL Peter Woods (neck) QUESTIONABLE

Bills: CB Christian Benford (groin), Dalton Kincaid (thumb, ankle), DT T.J. Sanders (shoulder), G O'Cyrus Torrence (ankle), LB Dorian Williams (calf) QUESTIONABLE

For the third straight week, the Chiefs will be without Kenneth Walker III. The star back continues to deal with a groin injury and, after practicing on a limited basis on Tuesday, did not participate on Wednesday. Emmett Johnson will once again assume the role as Kansas City's lead back.

After missing Monday's session, Bills corner Christian Benford logged back-to-back limited days of practice and is officially questionable to play. Meanwhile, Kincaid, Sanders, Torrence and Williams were limited throughout the week.

Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers

The Broncos have already ruled out safety Taylor Rapp and defensive end Sai'vion Jones (hamstring) for this Black Friday matchup with Pittsburgh. Elsewhere, the roster is pretty healthy as running back Tyler Badie (thumb), wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) and safety JL Skinner (shoulder) were all full participants on Wednesday.

Linebacker Alex Highsmith (ankle) and receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) both did not practice on Wednesday due to injury. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Cameron Heyward was given a rest day. Safety DeShon Elliott (knee), linebacker Nick Herbig (hip, ribs), and linebacker Cole Holcomb (heel) were all limited.

New Orleans Saints at Cincinnati Bengals

Tight end Juwan Johnson was the lone player missing from practice as he deals with a hamstring and wrist injury. Guard David Edwards (hamstring), offensive tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), center Erik McCoy (biceps), offensive tackle Asim Richards (knee) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) were limited.

The Bengals gave defensive tackle Jonathan Allen a rest day, so he was not at practice on Wednesday. Guard Dalton Risner was held out with a knee injury.

New York Giants at Indianapolis Colts

Pass rusher Abdul Carter did not practice on Wednesday due to ankle and calf injuries. John Harbaugh said Carter is day-to-day, but should play this weekend. Defensive tackle Shelby Harris and corner Andru Phillips also missed practice due to illness. Tight end Isaiah Likely (groin) and linebacker Arvell Reese (back) were limited.

Tight end Will Mallory (hamstring), running back Seth McGowan (hamstring), tight end Andrew Ogletree (knee), defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf), offensive tackle Jalen Travis (knee), and corner Charvarius Ward (knee) all missed Wednesday's practice for the Colts.

New York Jets at Miami Dolphins

Rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle, groin) and defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle) were held out of Wednesday's practice for the Jets. Receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs), offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee) and edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle, foot) were limited.

Miami held out corner Julius Brents (neck, shoulder), punter Bradley Pinion (right groin) and receiver Jared Wayne (quad) from the opening practice of the week. Linebacker Ronnie Harrison (hamstring), offensive tackle Austin Jackson (elbow, knee), defensive end Rodney McGraw (shoulder), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder, groin) and linebacker Jackson Woodard (hand) were all limited.

Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota Vikings

Atlanta was without six players to begin the week of practice: receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring), receiver Jahan Dotson (hamstring), safety DeMarcco Hellams (foot), guard Matthew Bergeron (hamstring), defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and defensive end Za'Darius Smith (rest). Defensive end James Pearce (back) was limited.

The Vikings held a walk-through practice, so the initial injury report is an estimate. That said, receiver Jordan Addison (thumb), offensive tackle Christian Darrisaw (shoulder), defensive lineman Jalen Redmond (ankle), corner Isaiah Rodgers (thigh), and safety Harrison Smith (thigh) were held out. Receiver Tai Felton (hip), quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) and receiver Myles Price (knee, groin) were limited.

Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars

Safety Terrell Burgess (knee), corner Cor'Dale Flott (neck) and offensive tackle Dan Moore Jr. (knee) were listed as non-participants at practice for the Titans. Defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers (back) was limited.

Running back Bhayshul Tuten was the only Jaguars player held out of Wednesday's practice as he deals with an ankle/foot injury. Defensive tackle Matt Dickerson (neck), linebacker Dennis Gardeck (neck), offensive lineman Robert Hainsey (knee), offensive tackle Walker Little (knee, receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle, offensive lineman Jonah Monheim (ankle), defensive end Danny Striggow (concussion), offensive lineman Cole Van Lanen (ankle) and offensive lineman Patrick Mekari (back) were all limited.

Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans

Defensive lineman Calais Campbell (rest, ribs), safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), and defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) did not practice with the Ravens on Wednesday. Meanwhile, receiver Rashod Bateman (groin), receiver Zay Flowers (ankle), outside linebacker Mike Green (knee), running back Derrick Henry (concussion), defensive lineman Aeneas Peebles (elbow) and guard John Simpson (groin) were all limited.

Receiver Kayshon Boutte (hip), defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring), tight end Brevin Jordan (finger, foot), defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins (ankle), and offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (neck, shoulder) were held out of practice by the Texans. Defensive tackle Logan Hall (hip, shoulder), receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) and linebacker Jake Hummel (abdomen, groin) were limited.

New England Patriots at Los Angeles Chargers

As expected, quarterback Drake Maye (fibula) and wide receiver A.J. Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday. The Patriots also held out corner Carlton Davis III (knee) and offensive lineman Walter Rouse (concussion protocol). On a more positive note, receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and left guard Alijah Vera-Trucker (hamstring), who are both on injured reserve but had their practice windows open, were limited.

The Chargers' list of players held out of Wednesday's practice is long. Quarterback Justin Herbert (concussion), outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle), corner Tarheeb Still (ankle), linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee), tight end David Njoku (shoulder), outside linebacker Akheem Mesidor (ankle), running back Keaton Mitchell (knee), defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (knee), corner Deane Leonard (groin), receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) and safety Kendall Williamson (calf) were all held out due to injury.

Washington Commanders at Arizona Cardinals

Washington listed Stefon Diggs as a non-participant during Wednesday's practice due to personal reasons. The only other player to miss the session was corner Amik Robertson due to an ankle injury. Receiver Treylon Burks (foot) and defensive end Charles Omenihu (rib) were limited.

Safety Budda Baker, offensive lineman Isaac Seumalo, center Hjalte Froholdt, and outside linebacker Josh Sweat were all given rest days and did not practice. Quarterback Carson Beck (back) did not practice, nor did guard Jon Gaines II (ankle). Linebackers Cody Simon (calf) and Mack Wilson Sr. (rest) were limited.

Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers

After missing two games due to quad and rib injuries, Sam Darnold returned to practice on Wednesday, and coach Mike Macdonald said he is on track to start, provided practice goes well. Macdonald also said that guard Quenton Nelson (knee) will be out again this week, but he's close to a return. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams, who missed the last two games with a stinger, was limited on Wednesday.

Quarterback Brock Purdy did not practice for the 49ers on Wednesday due to an ankle injury. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Purdy suffered the injury in the second quarter of last week's win over the Vikings and was able to finish the game. On top of Purdy, receiver Mike Evans (Achilles), receiver Jordan Watkins (groin), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) and safety Siran Neal (knee, foot) were held out of practice. Corners Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) were limited, along with offensive linemen Carver Willis (illness) and Austen Pleasants (knee).

Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns

The Raiders have listed Brock Bowers as a limited participant during Wednesday's practice as the tight end continues to deal with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) was also limited, while defensive tackles Adam Butler (concussion) and Tim Keenan (knee) did not practice.

Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'Dale Flott did not practice on Nov. 25 due to a neck injury he suffered against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 11.

Titans safety Terrell Burgess (knee) also didn't practice, according to the team's injury report, but safety Tony Adams (illness) was a full participant after missing the Cowboys game.

Secondary depth is a focus for Tennessee (1-9) ahead of its Week 12 game at the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) on Nov. 29 (noon CT, FOX). The Titans have struggled covering the field and were lit up by Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, surrendering 325 yards passing and four touchdowns.

Titans cornerback Micah Robinson struggled at times after replacing Flott.

Tennessee signed cornerback Corey Thornton off the Carolina Panthers' practice squad on Nov. 25. Thornton was activated to Carolina's 53-man roster twice this season and has eight tackles, one interception and three passes defensed in two games.

"Big, long, corner (who's) instinctive," Titans coach Robert Saleh said. "Excited to get him in here and see what he's got."

In other injury news, right guard Fernando Carmona Jr. (ankle) was a full practice participant a week after being designated to return from the injured reserve. Tackle Dan Moore Jr. (knee) did not practice.

Receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) and safety Kevin Winston Jr. (shoulder) were both full participants.

title: Bears rule out Gordon for second straight game due to shoulder injury - ESPN
authors: Courtney Cronin, Tim McManus, Todd Archer, Kevin Seifert, Daniel Oyefusi, Jamison Hensley, Mike Kaye, Rich Cimini, Liz Loza, Mike Clay
description:
CHICAGO -- Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon will miss Chicago's key NFC North game at Detroit on Thanksgiving due to a stubborn left shoulder injury.
Gordon has not practiced since before Chicago's Week 10 bye.
It is the first Thanksgiving Day game in NFL history between teams that have won at least five straight games.
The Bears are also set to be without running back Roschon Johnson, who left last Sunday's game on a cart with an ankle injury.
Salvon Ahmed was elevated from the practice squad for a third straight game.
text:
CHICAGO -- Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon will miss Chicago's key NFC North game at Detroit on Thanksgiving due to a stubborn left shoulder injury.

Gordon was listed as DNP for three straight days as the Bears conducted walk-throughs ahead of Thursday's game pitting two teams on a tear and tied in the division with 8-2 records. Coach Ben Johnson initially classified Gordon's injury as "day-to-day" in nature before ruling him out Wednesday. Johnson has not provided updates on the severity when asked about it late last week. Gordon has not practiced since before Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Thursday marks one of the most consequential Bears-Lions games in years. It is the first Thanksgiving Day game in NFL history between teams that have won at least five straight games. Chicago has racked up its streak since quarterback Caleb Williams returned from a hamstring injury in Week 6 and has not trailed in any game.

Meanwhile, Detroit is riding a six-game winning streak and is undefeated at home this season. This marks the 21st time the Bears and Lions have met on the holiday, with Chicago holding an 11-9 record over the last 20 Thanksgiving games.

Injuries have once again hit the Bears' secondary ahead of a pivotal division game on a short week. Safety Elijah Hicks was ruled out Tuesday with a concussion while cornerback Tyrique Stevenson was a late addition to Wednesday's injury report with a groin injury. Stevenson is considered questionable for Week 12.

Gordon made his 2026 season debut in Atlanta on Oct. 18 after missing the entire spring offseason program and training camp with a calf injury. He was one of Chicago's most productive defenders from Weeks 6-9 where he registered 4.0 sacks, 13 tackles (5 TFLs), 2 forced fumbles and a pass defensed.

His late arrival to the season stemmed from a calf injury that forced him to miss all of spring workouts and training camp. He was placed on the physically unable to perform list as the Bears formed their initial 53-man roster and spent time away from the team to rehab his injury before returning to practice on Sept. 30.

The Bears are also set to be without running back Roschon Johnson, who left last Sunday's game on a cart with an ankle injury. Salvon Ahmed was elevated from the practice squad for a third straight game. This will be Ahmed's third and final elevation before the Bears must sign him to the active roster.

title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy has ankle injury, won't practice Wednesday - ESPN
authors: Nick Wagoner, Anthony Gharib, Tim McManus, Todd Archer, Kevin Seifert, Daniel Oyefusi, Jamison Hensley, Mike Kaye, Rich Cimini, Liz Loza
description:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy will not practice Wednesday as he deals with an ankle injury suffered in Sunday night's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
According to coach Kyle Shanahan, Purdy injured his ankle in the second quarter and finished the game without issue.
But Purdy's ankle felt bad enough Wednesday that he will be a nonparticipant in the first practice of the week leading to Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.
Tight end George Kittle said he was not aware of Purdy's ankle injury during the game but didn't seem overly concerned about it Wednesday afternoon.
Elsewhere Wednesday, the 49ers activated defensive back Nate Hobbs from injured reserve and placed right tackle Colton McKivitz on injured reserve with a fractured and dislocated left ankle.
text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy will not practice Wednesday as he deals with an ankle injury suffered in Sunday night's game against the Minnesota Vikings.

According to coach Kyle Shanahan, Purdy injured his ankle in the second quarter and finished the game without issue. But Purdy's ankle felt bad enough Wednesday that he will be a nonparticipant in the first practice of the week leading to Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.

"When he can't go today, it's always a possibility [that his availability for Sunday could be in doubt]," Shanahan said. "It's not a high ankle, so it's day to day with it. But we've got to see how it goes."

A review of the game showed that Purdy had his foot and ankles spatted (athletic taped wrapped over a player's sock and cleat over the ankle to add extra support) for the final two quarters.

Shanahan said he knew of the injury when it happened, but it didn't affect his playcalling or the offensive approach for the rest of his team's 35-10 win. Purdy finished 21 of 26 for 255 yards and three touchdowns and earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors Wednesday.

Tight end George Kittle said he was not aware of Purdy's ankle injury during the game but didn't seem overly concerned about it Wednesday afternoon.

"He's a competitor," Kittle said. "He's going to play through things that none of us know about. That's an NFL football player. You play through things."

Mac Jones will take the reps with the first-team offense Wednesday and would be in line to start if Purdy is unable to play against Seattle. Kurtis Rourke is the Niners' other available quarterback option on the roster.

Elsewhere Wednesday, the 49ers activated defensive back Nate Hobbs from injured reserve and placed right tackle Colton McKivitz on injured reserve with a fractured and dislocated left ankle.

Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell was listed as a full participant on Wednesday and does not have a game status going into Week 12.

That means Mitchell is fully expected to play against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving.

That’s certainly good news for the Eagles as they try to slow down one of the best offenses in the NFL with an elite receiver duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Mitchell hurt his hamstring against the Steelers. He was listed as a non-participant to start the week, limited on Tuesday and full on Wednesday.

The Eagles aren’t practicing this week — they are holding walkthroughs — so all of these injury reports have been estimations.

They did rule out two players for Thursday’s game: OLB Arnold Ebiketie (oblique) and CB Jonathan Jones (ankle). Everyone else on the 53-man roster is good to go.

Both Ebiketie and Jones played against the Steelers on Sunday. Jones played well on Sunday when he took over for Riq Woolen but then got hurt on some friendly fire from safety Drew Mukuba.

The Chicago Bears have released their final injury report ahead of Thursday’s game against the Detroit Lions.

That report includes three players who have been ruled out for the Thanksgiving contest, including defensive back Kyler Gordon, who will miss his second straight game with a shoulder injury.

Gordon would not have practiced at all this week for the Bears, and now he officially has been ruled out for the critical NFC North showdown against the Lions.

Joining Gordon on the sidelines will be defensive back Elijah Hicks, who entered the NFL’s concussion protocol on Tuesday and will not suit up for Chicago on Thanksgiving in Detroit.

Running back Roschon Johnson, who was carted off the field during Sunday’s win over the New Orleans Saints with a toe injury, will also not play, according to the Bears.

Two Bears players were also listed as questionable for Thursday’s game, including defensive back Tyrique Stevenson, who was added to the team’s injury report Wednesday with a groin injury.

Linebacker D’Marco Jackson is also questionable with an elbow injury, though the Bears estimate he would have been able to fully participate in practice throughout the week leading up to the game.

Kickoff between the Bears and Lions is set for noon, with the game airing on CBS.

title: NFL Injury Report: Super Bowl MVP Begins Practice, Drake Maye's Return Uncertain & More
description:
Here’s a look at the major NFL injuries ahead of Week 12.
Terrance Ferguson (Rams, ankle/hamstring): Head coach Sean McVay has confirmed that Ferguson will have season-ending ankle surgery.
Defensive Standouts and Notable IR Updates Several significant defensive upgrades and injured reserve moves also impact the Week 12 picture.
He is officially listed as questionable after limited practice participation Sunday and Monday but is expected to make his 2026 season debut Wednesday.
What to Watch Before Week 12 Kickoff Wednesday night’s Packers-Rams clash kicks off Week 12 with Micah Parsons set to debut and Josh Jacobs carrying a questionable tag.
text:
With the 2026 regular season well into its Thanksgiving stretch and every team active on the schedule, injuries to key starters are forcing coaches and fantasy managers to make quick decisions. With Thanksgiving games looming, several key starters face availability questions that will reshape fantasy lineups and playoff positioning.

The Chargers-Patriots matchup hinges on Herbert’s concussion clearance; the Bills-Chiefs game on Walker’s groin recovery. The Thanksgiving slate arrives with four Pro Bowl-caliber starters in limbo, forcing coaches to gamble on availability hours before kickoff. Here’s a look at the major NFL injuries ahead of Week 12.

ADVERTISEMENT

Quarterbacks

QB health is going to be one of the big stories going into Week 12, with a number of teams relying on their backups or keeping a close eye on their concussion protocols.

Drake Maye (Patriots, fibula/ankle): Drake Maye’s fractured fibula will sideline him for at least six weeks, forcing the Patriots to turn to Tommy DeVito. The injury doesn’t require surgery, but Vrabel’s decision to keep Maye on the active roster signals confidence in a mid-season return—a massive blow to the Patriots’ skill-player ceiling in the interim. Vrabel confirmed on Monday that Maye won’t be playing in Week 12 against the Chargers, although the team would like to give him a chance to return later in the season. Tommy DeVito is set to start in Week 12 at QB. Maye’s absence is going to be a massive blow to the fantasy ceiling of the Patriots’ skill players.

ADVERTISEMENT

Justin Herbert (Chargers, concussion): Herbert went into the NFL concussion protocol after the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets. He took a sack on the Chargers’ final drive, then scrambled and threw a TD to Ladd McConkey. His participation in practice this week will be the deciding factor as to whether he clears the protocol in time to face the Patriots on Sunday.

ADVERTISEMENT

Patrick Mahomes (Chiefs, knee/right elbow) and Dak Prescott (Cowboys, left hand): Both are trending towards full availability for Thanksgiving. Mahomes was a full participant in KC’s Monday walkthrough and Tuesday practice despite having knee and right elbow listings going into Thursday’s game in Buffalo. Prescott was also a full participant in Dallas’ Tuesday walkthrough report with a left hand injury prior to their game against Philadelphia.
